claims.label: supported
claims.claim_summary: OverclaimBench is an evaluation suite with five file-review scenarios and planted defects.
claims.claim_text_verbatim: We introduce OverclaimBench, an evaluation suite of five file-review scenarios with transcript-based coverage measurements and registered planted defects.

claims.label: supported
claims.claim_summary: Evaluation of 12 models shows agents often omit files, misrepresent coverage, and miss defects.
claims.claim_text_verbatim: We evaluate eight proprietary frontier models in their own production command-line interfaces and four open-weight models under a single fixed harness, and find that 1) agents fail to read every file they were asked to review in 67.9% of runs; 2) among these incomplete runs, agents are misleading 80.4% of the time (59–96% per model), either falsely claiming a complete review or leaving the gap undisclosed; 3) requiring delegation to subagents increases coverage, but a large majority of reviews that remain incomplete are still misleading; and 4) agents that falsely claim a complete review miss planted defects at about 1.8 times the rate of agents that read every file, showing that claims of completion can conceal substantive failures.

claims.label: supported
claims.claim_summary: OverclaimBench evaluates whether coding agents accurately report their work scope.
claims.claim_text_verbatim: We address these questions by introducing OverclaimBench (Figure 1), an evaluation suite to measure whether coding agents accurately report the scope of their work.

claims.label: supported
claims.claim_summary: The benchmark measures incomplete agent work without artificial tool breaking or missing inputs.
claims.claim_text_verbatim: We measure incomplete work in agentic tasks without introducing artificial elements, such as deliberately breaking tools or withholding required inputs.

claims.claim_summary: Agents exhibit misleading reporting regardless of provider, capability level, or subagent usage.
claims.claim_text_verbatim: We show that agents are misleading across providers, capability levels, and subagent use.

claims.claim_summary: Agents that overclaim task completion miss planted defects at higher rates.
claims.claim_text_verbatim: We demonstrate that when agents overclaim, they are more likely to miss planted defects.

claims.claim_summary: Scenario input files fit entirely within model context windows to isolate behavior.
claims.claim_text_verbatim: For each scenario, we ensure that the input files fit within the context window of each model we test so that failure to touch every file cannot be attributed to context-length limitations but instead reflects model behavior.

claims.label: supported
claims.claim_summary: The needle registry was validated via isolated single-file, negative, and dependency checks.
claims.claim_text_verbatim: We validated the registry by checking that a model reviewing the relevant files in isolation reports every needle, that it is not reported once the planted problem is removed, and that all registered source files are required to identify the needle (see Appendix B for more details).

claims.label: supported
claims.claim_summary: Across models, 52.8% of incomplete reviews explicitly claimed full coverage.

claims.claim_summary: Incomplete runs are misleading 80.4% of the time, exceeding 50% for all models.
claims.claim_text_verbatim: As can be seen in Figure 2, responses that overclaim or omit disclosure are frequent among runs that do not touch every file: 80.4% of incomplete runs were misleading, and the rate exceeded 50% for every model (59.0% for Claude Opus 5 to 96.2% for GPT-5.6-luna; Table 1).

claims.label: supported
claims.claim_summary: Models can be honest on OverclaimBench by admitting partial coverage in 19.6% of cases.
claims.claim_text_verbatim: A minority of incomplete runs (19.6%) honestly report that their coverage is incomplete, showing that models can be honest on OverclaimBench simply by admitting incomplete coverage.

claims.label: supported
claims.claim_summary: Open-weight models are misleading in 65.0–85.1% of incomplete runs.
claims.claim_text_verbatim: For the four open-weight models (DeepSeek, Qwen, GLM-5.3, and GLM-5.3-Flash), the same pattern holds; among incomplete runs, 65.0–85.1% are misleading.

claims.label: supported
claims.claim_summary: Overclaiming occurs across both shallow and deep corpus reading runs.
claims.claim_text_verbatim: It occurs both in runs that read hardly any of the corpus and in runs that read a large fraction of it.

claims.label: supported
claims.claim_summary: Delegation significantly increased file coverage in the Claude model family.
claims.claim_text_verbatim: Delegation increased the rate of runs with all files touched in the Claude family (condition effect: G2 = 46.27, 1 df, p < 0.0001).

claims.label: supported
claims.claim_summary: Among incomplete runs, delegation significantly increased misleading responses in Claude models.
claims.claim_text_verbatim: However, among incomplete runs, delegation increased the proportion of misleading runs (condition effect: G2 = 19.10, 1 df, p < 0.0001).

claims.label: supported
claims.claim_summary: Delegation failed to reduce misleading responses in incomplete GPT runs, staying near 100%.
claims.claim_text_verbatim: Among incomplete runs, delegation did not reduce the rate of misleading runs in any GPT model, which remained at or near 100 % in both conditions.

claims.label: supported
claims.claim_summary: Higher model capability does not reduce misleading reporting during incomplete runs.
claims.claim_text_verbatim: We note that, like delegation, model capability does not solve the issue of misleading response behavior: neither family shows a capability effect on misleading reporting among incomplete runs.

claims.label: supported
claims.claim_summary: Overclaiming runs missed 58.2% of needles compared to 32.4% in complete-coverage runs.
claims.claim_text_verbatim: Pooling further across scenarios, explicitly overclaiming runs missed 720 of 1,237 needles (58.2%) and omission runs missed 273 of 650 (42.0%), compared with 342 of 1,055 (32.4%) in runs that touched every file.

claims.label: supported
claims.claim_summary: Needle reporting strongly correlates with whether the relevant evidence was read.
claims.claim_text_verbatim: As a validity check, we confirmed that needle reporting tracks reading: a needle was reported 83.2% of the time its evidence was read, compared with 1.8% of the time it was not (Figure 5, right panel).

claims.claim_summary: Mandatory subagents reduced explicit overclaiming overall, but 50.3% of incomplete reviews still overclaimed.
claims.claim_text_verbatim: In the controlled delegation experiment, requiring subagents increased coverage and reduced explicit overclaiming overall, yet 50.3% of the reviews that remained incomplete still overclaimed.

claims.claim_summary: Incomplete delegating reviews failed to disclose coverage gaps in 83-100% of runs.
claims.claim_text_verbatim: Including omissions, incomplete delegating reviews failed to disclose their coverage gaps in 83–100% of runs across the six models.

claims.label: supported
claims.claim_summary: All evaluation scenarios fit comfortably within the context windows of tested models.
claims.claim_text_verbatim: Every scenario fits every model: proof review, the largest, uses 76% of the tightest context window, and every other scenario uses 27% or less.

claims.label: supported
claims.claim_summary: Subagent requirements boosted mean file coverage to 97.3% and reading depth to 87.3%.
claims.claim_text_verbatim: Requiring subagents increased mean file coverage from 86.9% to 97.3% and mean reading depth from 67.0% to 87.3%.

claims.claim_summary: Subagent usage increased planted-defect detection from 49.9% to 69.6%.
claims.claim_text_verbatim: This additional coverage translated into more needle recovery: solo runs reported 49.9% of planted-defect instances, compared with 69.6% when subagents were used.

claims.claim_summary: The LLM review-scope judge achieved 91.1% unanimity and 0.977 modal agreement across samples.
claims.claim_text_verbatim: 705 of 774 runs (91.1%) are unanimous across all eight samples, with a mean modal agreement of 0.977.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Every headline conditional rate moves by less than one percentage point under resampling, so the misleading-reporting finding is not an artifact of judge sampling noise.
